bluf: Blue Array is a founder led organic search specialist in Reading selling SEO, digital PR and GEO through a consultancy agency hybrid it calls consulgency. The record shows it pushing AI visibility: a dedicated GEO page, 12 AI search URLs and banking, property and retail AI visibility reports promoted by 24 LinkedIn company ads. It lists no dated moves and its sitemap shows 0 URLs updated in 90 days. The one thing a rival should know: all 17 clients on record are names only, so the book is likely contestable on evidence of work, while the Horus read puts it Favored at 28.3 with measurement (KJ9) as its exposure.
doing:
Blue Array sells organic search in three lines and calls the way it sells them consulgency, a registered term for a consultancy agency hybrid; in plain words it offers advice and execution under one contract and positions the whole as search that converts. Its headline claim is that it is the UK's leading SEO, GEO and digital PR agency, and the one figure it leads with is an Ignite case citing +327% organic clicks year on year.

The capability evidence sits on the three lines it leads with. SEO scores 3: the title and H1 present a specialist, market leading organic search agency. Content & Digital PR scores 3: the meta names Digital PR in its lead claim and a brand first Digital PR page sits beside a content service. AI Search / GEO scores 3: GEO is in the homepage title with a dedicated GEO page and 12 AI search URLs. The record lists twelve services, two proprietary products (consulgency and Ignite, a 12 month startup and scale up programme) and no partners.

Its AI posture is commercial rather than operational: it sells GEO for ChatGPT, Gemini and Llama citations, publishes AI visibility studies of banks, property and retail brands, and promotes them through LinkedIn ads; AI Automation / Agents scores 0.

The record lists no dated moves, news items or job postings; the status note says the score comes from an April 2026 Internet Archive capture and the live site was not read. Pricing signals are partial: CRO is sold as packages or a retainer, audits as packages, Ignite as a fixed 12 month programme with free quotes, and no prices were captured. Conspicuously absent for a search agency of its kind: paid search, paid social, programmatic, data and measurement, email and CRM and web build all score 0, and no case study in the record describes the work behind any client.
clients:
The record marks its client type as mixed and lists eight verticals: banking and payments, finance and fintech, insurance and insurtech, education, software and training, retail and fashion, media and publishing, property and automotive. The home market is the UK, with Reading the only office listed.

The book holds 17 named clients and every one is a name only: 16 come from case study slugs on its portfolio pages and 1 (Zigzag) from the Ignite page, none carries a title or a described result, so each need is inferred from the sold mix rather than observed. On that basis the retail and fashion names Accessorize, Monsoon, Boden, River Island and Depop, the finance names TransferGo, GoCardless and Funding Circle, the property and automotive names Zoopla and Carwow, the media name Daily Mail, and Post Office, RAC, Help for Heroes and Floom would most likely have come for organic demand and for PR, reputation and content, the lines it leads with; the record does not say so for any of them.

One client is shared with another tracked agency: Moonpig also appears on the book of kaizen. The record names no other overlap.

What the base needs next is a judgment. The edition's KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) is the judgment it is best placed for, and its own banking and retail AI visibility reports suggest it is already selling that need back to its clients; it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the retail and finance names ask for citation share and AI visibility measurement next, and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) makes it a roughly even chance that they get an audited number, since data and measurement scores 0 in its record.

No Meta or TikTok check is recorded.
market:
The Horus read puts Blue Array at a tailwind index of 28.3, band Favored, resilience 26.9. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) at net 0.438, driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and for KJ8 at 0.281; it is most exposed to KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) at -0.219, driven by SEO. The best scenario fit is The Toll Road at 67/100. It is making P1 (audited AI visibility) and P5 (outcome pricing); P2 (feeds and entities), P6 (agent operators) and P7 (owned audience hedges) are absent; P3, P4 and P8 do not apply.

The Monsoon read is 57.5, band Onshore wind, migration 56.0 against displacement 59.0, an inferred class. 56 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (22) and Content & Digital PR (14) carrying the most movable hours; the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia, 20% to Eastern Europe and 15% to Africa and the Maghreb. No hub offices or onshore claims are listed, so the footprint is inferred.
openings:
The strongest opening is the book itself: 17 of 17 clients are names without described work, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival bringing a described result in retail and fashion or in finance can contest Accessorize, Boden, River Island, Depop, TransferGo, GoCardless or Funding Circle on evidence. The falsifier is a live Blue Array case study page describing measurable work for any of them.

The gap to lead with is machine readable work: P2 is absent, with no feed, schema or entity work in the record on its core search line, so a rival that packages schema, feeds and entities as the delivery layer under GEO very likely undercuts a GEO offer sold on reports and events. The contradiction to press: it sells content and digital PR while its own sitemap shows 0 updates in 90 days.

The judgment exposure is KJ9: its SEO hours are the ones measurement trouble removes and data and measurement scores 0, so an offer priced on audited citation share and organic outcomes is likely to win that conversation. Moonpig, shared with kaizen, is the one client shopping.
